clue.text: Belt components the wrong way round

indicators.note: the wrong way round tells us to write the word for components backwards

parts.note: components are the parts that make something up

explanation.surface: Someone has fitted the pieces of a belt back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way round' reverses PARTS to give STRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A belt is a band of leather or fabric, which is a kind of strap.

clue.text: Relative by marriage continues to make strides?

definitions.meaning: a spouse's son from an earlier relationship
read as two words: keeps on walking forward

explanation.surface: A family member who just keeps walking on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as STEPS ON for the second reading; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband's or wife's son from a previous union becomes a family member through marriage.

clue.text: Lover married after a break-up

indicators.note: a break-up smashes the word married apart so its letters can be put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A sweetheart who was once married, now divorced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a break-up' rearranges the letters of MARRIED into ADMIRER.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is someone who is fond of or romantically drawn to another person, a lover.

clue.text: General award

definitions.meaning: Ulysses S. ..., Union general in the American Civil War
a sum of money awarded, or the verb to give

explanation.walkthrough: 'General' is a capitalised rank pointing at a famous American commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses Grant led the Union armies; separately a grant is money given or awarded by a body.

clue.text: South American animal getting cold in the Far East?

indicators.note: in says the word for cold sits inside the Far Eastern country

parts.note: China is a country of the Far East
a chill is a cold

explanation.surface: A South American creature catching a cold on a trip to Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting cold' reads as catching a chill; 'in' is the insertion signal, with the country split around the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinchilla is a small furry rodent native to the Andes mountains.

clue.text: On vessel, a bit of a looker

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
a tin is a container

explanation.surface: A cryptic aside about an attractive person on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a looker' tempts as a beautiful person; here the looker is the eye, and the retina is one part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye, a part of what looks.

clue.text: A shade old, compass

parts.note: compass means scope or extent, a range

explanation.surface: A faded old colour on a compass card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compass' means extent here, not the navigation instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange is a colour, and a shade is a particular hue.

clue.text: Potential trouble in bonkers family

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A crazy family is likely to cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana skin is a figurative hazard, something that could trip you up and cause embarrassment.

clue.text: One held by facial feature, sound

indicators.note: held by puts the numeral for one inside the facial feature

parts.note: the nose is a feature of the face
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone held by the nose makes a sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' puts I inside NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A noise is any sound, especially a loud one.

clue.text: University study

definitions.meaning: the University of ..., in the English town of that name
... a subject is studying it at university

explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a town west of London with a well-known university; British students 'read' a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense names a British university town; the other is the act of studying books.

clue.text: Under the table, unlike tables?

definitions.meaning: too drunk to stand, slang for very drunk

explanation.walkthrough: Legless is British slang for extremely drunk; the second reading takes it literally, as having no legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under the table is being drunk enough to collapse; tables stand on legs.

clue.text: Almost missing the front, definitely not behind!

indicators.note: missing the front says the first letter of the word for almost drops away

parts.note: nearly means almost

explanation.surface: An exclamation about being almost but not quite late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing the front' drops the N from NEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ahead of time is the opposite of being behind schedule or late.

clue.text: Cleaner TV show

definitions.meaning: a ... opera, a long-running serial drama

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like a person; it is the washing product.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap washes things clean; a soap opera is a long-running television drama.

clue.text: Behind spirit, phantom's head

parts.note: rum is a spirit drink

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word phantom's

explanation.surface: A ghost's head seen behind another spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests a ghost alongside the phantom, but it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The rump is the backside or buttocks, so a noun for one's behind.

clue.text: Rebuilt Pantheon about right for old temple

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the abbreviation for right
rebuilt says the letters of Pantheon are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: The Roman Pantheon reconstructed to become another ancient temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebuilt' rearranges PANTHEON to PATHENON; 'about' puts it round R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parthenon is the ancient Greek temple to Athena on the Acropolis in Athens.

clue.text: March, perhaps, or bound

definitions.meaning: March is an example of a month in that season

explanation.walkthrough: 'March' tempts as a verb to walk; it is the month, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: March falls in the season after winter; to leap or jump is a synonym of bound.

clue.text: Breakfast item found in nutmeg grater

indicators.note: found in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A breakfast item turns up in the kitchen grater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' points to EGG spanning nutmEG Grater.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg is a staple breakfast food, boiled, fried or scrambled.

clue.text: Famous fish is a bird!

parts.note: star as an adjective means famous, a star player
a ling is an edible sea fish

explanation.surface: A celebrity fish turns out to be a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The starling is a common songbird with glossy speckled plumage.

clue.text: Compound sat with inert compounds

indicators.note: to compound is to mix together, so the letters of sat and inert are combined in a new order

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about a compound sitting with unreactive ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' looks like the definition; it is a verb, the anagram signal, and the final 'compounds' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrates are chemical salts containing the nitrate ion, a class of compounds.

clue.text: Raunchier dancing that will sweep you off your feet!

definitions.text: that will sweep you off your feet!

indicators.note: dancing has the letters of Raunchier moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: More suggestive dancing that will sweep you off your feet romantically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges RAUNCHIER. The definition reads as romance but means a literal blowing over.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurricane is a violent tropical storm whose winds can knock a person over.

clue.text: Court hearing involving something sticky?

indicators.note: involving says the sticky thing is held inside the hearing

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing
a sticky bun is an iced sweet roll

explanation.surface: A court case concerning something sticky.
explanation.walkthrough: A sticky bun is a sweet glazed roll; 'involving' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a body set up to judge disputes, a kind of court.

clue.text: Very god boy accepts gift finally, a sovereign

definitions.note: the published clue drops a letter: it means very good

indicators.note: accepts says the boy takes in a letter

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of gift

parts.note: a king is a sovereign ruler

explanation.surface: A boy receives a present and turns out to be a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'god' is a typo for 'good'. STONKING is British slang for excellent. 'accepts' puts T inside SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonking is informal British slang meaning excellent or impressively great.

clue.text: Egyptian god, so coming up before Greek goddess

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the word so is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Iris is the Greek goddess of the rainbow

explanation.surface: An Egyptian deity rises before a Greek one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reverses SO to OS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the ancient Egyptian god of the afterlife and the dead.

clue.text: Does one secure a piece of wedding cake?

definitions.meaning: a person who ties things, read as one who fastens
one layer of a stacked cake

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the answer as TIE plus -ER, one who ties.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding cake is built in stacked layers; one who fastens knots is one who ties.

clue.text: Hideous thug, Lysander to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A brutish Lysander is described as hideous, after a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Hideous and its synonym both describe something very unpleasant to look at.

clue.text: One that can look both up and down

definitions.text: One that can look both up and down

parts.note: the organ of sight is what looks

indicators.note: both up and down says the down entry reads the same in either direction

explanation.surface: Something that can glance upward and downward.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface means gazing up and down; the wordplay means the letters read the same upwards as downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of sight is what any creature looks with.
